input.reasoning: No match found. I searched the claim as written and the proposed canonical form, colloquial paraphrases ("The Large Hadron Collider is safe", "LHC safety concerns are unfounded", "carries no risk of catastrophic harm"), the accelerator-and-operations framing ("Experiments at the LHC threaten public safety", "There are no reasons for concern about experiments at CERN's LHC"), and the negation/contrary direction in four variants ("The LHC could destroy the Earth", "could pose a danger to Earth", "poses a catastrophic risk to the planet", "will create dangerous black holes"), plus the physics-scenario vocabulary (strangelets) and the cosmic-ray safety comparison. All fourteen searches returned zero results, in both directions of the proposition, so the graph holds neither this claim nor its counterpart under any wording the retrieval surfaced; with no near-misses to weigh, there are no alternative matches. This is the LHC safety assertion (the CERN/LSAG position, published during the 2008 safety controversy). The source sentence carries two clauses ("present no danger" and "no reasons for concern"), but the second is the practical upshot of the first, not an independent proposition: the same considerations bear on both, so the instance records one voice on one claim, with the redundant clause living in the instance's verbatim text. I kept the proposed canonical form: it is terse, frame-independent, states the safety thesis affirmatively as the discourse's named position, and stays deliberately unsharpened ("danger" unqualified) where the public debate itself ranges unqualifiedly over the vague proposition. One relationship the Steward may want to capture at decomposition: the narrower, stronger doomsday proposition ("the LHC could destroy the Earth") is a close counterpart and, on my reading, a specification of this claim; if it is later minted, link it as such. Stance: the source asserts the safety proposition outright, so it affirms the claim as canonically stated. Confidence slightly below certainty because fourteen zero-hit searches establish non-existence only as strongly as embedding retrieval can; per the recoverable-error preference, creating is the safe side of any residual doubt.
input.direction_note: The safety conclusion is the named, published position in this discourse (the LHC safety assessments, cited and disputed widely), and it reads as a positive property assertion ("no danger", equivalent to "the LHC is safe") rather than a surface negation, so it is the canonical direction; sources alleging danger will be recorded as denials on this same node.
